name: liblqr
why: Seam carving is a fascinating content-aware resizing idea, though the library itself is a plain C/C++ dependency.

brief.what_it_is: Liquid Rescale Library (liblqr) is a free, open source C/C++ seam carving library. It implements the content-aware resizing algorithm from a paper by Shai Avidan and Ariel Shamir. Per the wiki, you give it a picture and a target size, and it resizes the image non-uniformly while trying to keep the important parts from distorting. The homepage says it also supports saving and loading carving information, real-time scaling, manual feature selection, and customizable progress reporting. The library requires glib-2.0 version 2.8 or later. The README-equivalent here is a Wikidot wiki, not a repository README, and it does not show input or output formats beyond that.
brief.why_it_exists: The wiki says the goal is to resize pictures non-uniformly while preserving their features, avoiding distortion of the important parts. It also says the API is meant to be 'powerful, yet fast and easy to use'.
brief.how_it_works: The wiki does not explain the mechanism beyond naming the Avidan and Shamir seam carving paper. It only says the library implements that algorithm.
brief.install_notes: The homepage requires glib-2.0 version 2.8. Windows users who only want the GIMP Liquid Rescale plug-in do not need the library, since the plug-in ships with it. The Download and Installation pages are linked from the wiki, but my guessed Installation and Features URLs returned 404, so I have no install steps beyond the glib requirement. The wiki says code hosting moved to GitHub in July 2014, but the page gives no URL for it, so I did not fetch the repository.
brief.standout: The library is used by several well-known open source projects, including the GIMP Liquid Rescale plug-in, digiKam, ImageMagick, and Photivo, according to the wiki. Its main draw is that it is a reusable C/C++ seam carving library rather than only an app feature.
brief.status: Last release on the homepage is version 0.4.3, dated Aug 30th, 2024. Before that, the News list shows releases 0.4.2 (Dec 2012), 0.4.1 (May 2009), and 0.4.0 (May 2009). The most recent news item is the July 2014 notice that code hosting moved to GitHub. The 2024 release date suggests it is still maintained, but I could not check a commit history or GitHub activity, so the status is unclear.
brief.caveats: Only the Wikidot homepage loaded. The Installation and Features pages returned HTTP 404 at the URLs I guessed, and I did not find the real links, so the API, platform support, and build steps are unverified. The wiki is licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 3.0. The scout note calls it a plain C/C++ dependency, which fits what I saw. The site is a wiki that says it is 'always in need of improvement'.
quotes: an easy to use C/C++ seam carving library
It is a free, open source implementation of the algorithm described in this paper by Shai Avidan and Ariel Shamir.
It aims at resizing pictures non uniformly while preserving their features, i.e. avoiding distortion of the important parts.
